items.auditor_proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY, adjudication routed onward: either respan Isa.33.1-Isa.33.24 as Isa.33.1-Isa.33.12 plus Isa.33.13-Isa.33.24, cutting at the verse-initial summons with the SAMEKH at MT 33:12 as tier-3 corroboration; or hold the span and re-argue the decline on a ground that survives the tier-1 imperative-onset and addressee-shift class and that also distinguishes MT 33:13 from the neighbouring onset at MT 34:1.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Every byte ground re-derives. The summons שִׁמְע֥וּ רְחוֹקִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֑יתִי (oshb:Isa.33.13, byte tier) is a verse-initial imperative with named addressees; that verse-initial imperative stands at exactly 10 MT verses book-wide, identical at skeleton and accent-stripped tiers (MT 1:2, 1:10, 33:13, 46:3, 46:12, 48:1, 49:1, 51:1, 51:7, 66:5), MT 33:13 the single chapters-28-35 site. The seg layer carries SAMEKH at MT 33:1, 33:6, 33:12. Under the convention this corpus itself applies -- the row reads the MT 32:20 seg as closing the preceding verse -- the MT 33:12 division falls immediately before the summons, so the row's claim that its interior segs mark turns binding 'to no fresh hoy or vocative marker of their own' is byte-false at exactly the declined site; it is true only at MT 33:6, whose next verse opens on the presentative הֵ֚ן אֶרְאֶלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.33.7, byte tier). The stated decline rule -- absence of a fresh hoy, massa, or divine-frame marker -- also fails to discriminate MT 33:13 from קִרְב֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ לִשְׁמֹ֔עַ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים הַקְשִׁ֑יבוּ (oshb:Isa.34.1, byte tier): first-token and koh-amar-bigram checks at skeleton tier find no hoy, massa, or koh-amar frame in either onset, the row itself calls the two the same formal class, and the neighbouring row cuts at MT 34:1; on the row's stated rule its own rear seam at MT 33:24, which carries no seg, is left without positive warrant. A whole-chapter span held by a decline that omits the tier-1 imperative-onset and addressee-shift class and rests on a byte-false mark-binding claim is a load-bearing defect: high as filed. Span ruling: endorse_proposal -- the respan case is byte-sound (a tier-1 summons onset at MT 33:13, the same signal class the sibling cuts at MT 32:9 and MT 34:1 rest on, with the MT 33:12 SAMEKH as tier-3 corroboration), and the proposal's alternative branch, holding the span under a re-argued decline that does distinguish MT 34:1's scene turn from the continuing Zion scene at MT 33:13-14, stays open to the owner docket; nothing adopted here.

Tested against the row: the boundary itself is byte-sound, since the tier-1 onset at 40.18 supports the same cut, so the defect is a defective warrant rather than a load-bearing one -- medium as filed. This is the same seam as the onset finding on the following row; one seam-pair edit cures both. Not a span item.

items.claim: A cross-seam device is dismissed as a rendering-level echo and declared not a recurrence in the Hebrew at any tier; re-collated, the shared interrogative particle recurs at accent_stripped tier in both directions, and the fourfold pattern the row calls a rendering fact is fourfold in the Hebrew bytes.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair, device_notes only: name the count object and restate at the collated tiers -- the clause-level comparison returns tier NONE while the shared interrogative particle re-collates at accent_stripped tier across the seam -- and drop 'rendering-level echo' for a Hebrew-side description. No span or seam change.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-collated at every tier. The row's sentence 'not a recurrence in the Hebrew at any tier' is byte-false at the particle level: הֲל֤וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.28 at accent_stripped tier, and הֲל֨וֹא (oshb:Isa.40.28, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.21 at accent_stripped tier, the two tokens differing only in cantillation. The fourfold pattern is in the Hebrew bytes, not in the rendering: הֲל֤וֹא, הֲל֣וֹא, הֲל֛וֹא, הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte, each against its own verse) -- four tokens of the one particle -- and the two verb roots recur in the same order across the seam, תֵֽדְעוּ֙ then תִשְׁמָ֔עוּ (oshb:Isa.40.21, tier: byte) against יָדַ֜עְתָּ then שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ (oshb:Isa.40.28, tier: byte), each against its own verse, in different persons and stems, so no contiguous-skeleton match between the pairs. The clause-level comparison is honestly tier NONE in both directions -- הֲל֤וֹא תֵֽדְעוּ֙ against oshb:Isa.40.28 and הֲל֨וֹא יָדַ֜עְתָּ אִם לֹ֣א שָׁמַ֗עְתָּ against oshb:Isa.40.21 both return none -- which is exactly what the following row states, clause against clause; this row's unqualified 'at any tier' and its 'rendering-level echo' label are the form the bytes refuse, and the negative names no count object. The device straddles the row's own close seam (oshb:Isa.40.21 inside, 40.28 outside), so the tier misstatement lands on a cross-seam cohesion disclosure; it does not disturb the boundary, which the imperative onset at oshb:Isa.40.26 and the envelope closure at 40.25 carry. Defective tier claim, not load-bearing: medium as filed. Not a span item.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the bytes and from the ruled strategy text. The operative-category law sits under the unit_type vocabulary ('each line above names the operative category, not an exclusive grant; any closed-vocabulary value applies wherever the row's own bytes carry that form, with a one-sentence deviation disclosure'); it governs which closed-vocabulary unit_type value a row may carry, not which signal class may carry a seam, so the device_notes appeal ('disclosed here per the operative-category allowance since no woe, massa, or divine-speech-frame formula opens or closes this span') does not license the construction as a boundary driver. Even read charitably as a salvation_oracle deviation disclosure, the same sentence expressly disclaims 'an imperative or addressee shift' as the boundary ground, and that disclaimed class stands in the onset verse's own bytes: the preceding material is unaddressed third person through נֶחְשְׁבוּ לֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.40.17, tier: byte), and the onset opens a second-person-plural address, תְּדַמְּי֣וּן and תַּ֥עַרְכוּ (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte, each against its own verse; web:Isa.40.18 'will you liken', 'will you compare'), continuing at oshb:Isa.40.21 and 40.25. The envelope the row argues is honest at its stated tiers -- וְאֶל מִ֖י (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.40.25 at accent_stripped tier, while the fuller clauses וְאֶל מִ֖י תְּדַמְּי֣וּן (oshb:Isa.40.18, tier: byte) and וְאֶל מִ֥י תְדַמְּי֖וּנִי (oshb:Isa.40.25, tier: byte) return none against each other in both directions -- so it is a matching two-word interrogative prefix, not a byte-identical refrain that the refrain-close law would let carry the seam by itself. observed_substrate_signals carries topic_onset, inclusio_bracket and postpositive_inquit, no addressee_shift. Boundary byte-sound; warrant grounded on a non-ruled class with a misapplied law citation: medium as filed. Same seam as the close finding on the preceding row; one seam-pair edit cures both. Not a span item.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the bytes and the mark inventory. The close as written: the only ground named at oshb:Isa.41.16|41.17 in boundary_rationale is 'sealed by a PE parashah mark (single-witness), backing the division there'; strongest_rejected_alternative argues only why the fear-not chain runs past 41.13 (an internal-cohesion point) and then calls both marks 'not as the deciding ground', which leaves no deciding ground named at all. The mark is real (inventory at MT keys: PE at 41:16, SAMEKH at 41:7 and 41:13, PE at 41:20, nothing at 41:17), but Prophets parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration, never a driver. oshb:Isa.41.17 appears in no field of the row (checked against boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, device_notes and all fourteen boundary_evidence_refs). The unnamed tier-1 ground is byte-present: the span is second person throughout -- וְאַתָּה֙ ... בְּחַרְתִּ֑יךָ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte, each against its own verse), אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.41.10, tier: byte), וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte) -- while oshb:Isa.41.17-41.20 carry no second-person form (first-person promises and third-person referents, read verse by verse against both witnesses; no morphology layer is staged, so this is a pointed-bytes-plus-rendering claim), so the addressee is dropped exactly at the close. The cross-seam title recurrence is also byte-true: קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Isa.41.14, tier: byte) collates against oshb:Isa.41.16 and against oshb:Isa.41.20 at skeleton tier (the 41.14 token carries meteg, retained at accent_stripped, so skeleton is the honest tier), בִּקְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte) against oshb:Isa.41.20 returns none, and the bare core קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.43.3, tier: byte) collates against both oshb:Isa.41.16 and 41.20 at byte tier; the row lists the three sites with tiers but never states that the recurrence into 41.20 leaves its close undisturbed, the sentence the following row does carry for the same pair. Boundary byte-sound on the addressee drop; the defect is the warrant (a tier-3 mark in the driver role) plus a disclosure gap: medium as filed. Not a span item.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the onset verse's own bytes. Every reference to the pair is third person: הָעֲנִיִּ֨ים וְהָאֶבְיוֹנִ֜ים מְבַקְשִׁ֥ים (oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte; plural participle subject), then לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם, אֶעֱנֵ֔ם and אֶעֶזְבֵֽם (oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte, each against its own verse; third-person-plural suffixes on a noun and on two first-person verbs), rendered 'their tongue', 'answer them', 'forsake them' at web:Isa.41.17. Read verse by verse, oshb:Isa.41.17-41.20 carries no second-person form (first-person verbs at 41.18-41.19, a third-person purpose clause at 41.20; both witnesses agree; no morphology layer is staged), whereas the preceding unit is second person from וְאַתָּה֙ (oshb:Isa.41.8, tier: byte) to וְאַתָּה֙ תָּגִ֣יל (oshb:Isa.41.16, tier: byte). So 'addressed to the same unnamed poor and needy without renaming the addressee' (boundary_rationale) and 'without renaming the addressee' (strongest_rejected_alternative) are byte-false form claims: the pair is a described referent, not an addressee, and the second-person addressee of the preceding unit is dropped at this seam rather than carried across. The divine-title clause in the same sentence is byte-true (אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל, oshb:Isa.41.17, tier: byte). Load-bearing test: the row's cut rests on the topic onset plus the PE mark (inventory re-read: PE at MT 41:16 and 41:20, nothing at 41:17); the false clause argues continuity against the row's own cut rather than carrying it, and the boundary is byte-sound on the very addressee drop the row misdescribes. Byte-false form claim inside the warrant, not alone load-bearing: medium as filed. Not a span item.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. The onset as written rests on a content characterisation ('a third-person divine presentation of an unnamed servant figure') plus the PE mark at MT 41:29 (inventory re-read: PE at 41:29 and 42:4; tier-3, never a driver), with no ruled frame class named; the close is tier-1 and exact -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte) -- and the koh-amar skeleton sweep over chs 41-43 returns exactly oshb:Isa.42.5, 43.1, 43.14 and 43.16 (sweep: 4 verses, none in ch 41, none of the four royal-messenger sites), so the digit holds. Under the ruled vocabulary the servant_song value applies only where the unit's bounds are argued from tier-1 seams, which the onset side does not do: the defect is real and medium as filed (the boundary is not byte-shown wrong, and the row already holds it at low confidence with the frontier flag set). One correction to the finding's grounds, which the remediation docket must carry: the trial speech's second-person-plural address is real -- רִֽיבְכֶ֖ם (oshb:Isa.41.21, tier: byte), הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם מֵאַ֔יִן (oshb:Isa.41.24, tier: byte), אִמְרֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.41.26, tier: byte) -- but it is not dropped at oshb:Isa.42.1: its last form is that 41.26 suffix, and oshb:Isa.41.27-41.29 already carry no second-person form (first-person verbs at 41.27-41.28; third-person plural מַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם and נִסְכֵּיהֶֽם at oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte, each against its own verse; read against both witnesses, no morphology layer staged). What the seam itself carries in the bytes is a presentative onset of a new referent -- הֵ֣ן כֻּלָּ֔ם (oshb:Isa.41.29, tier: byte) answered by הֵ֤ן עַבְדִּי֙ (oshb:Isa.42.1, tier: byte), the two particles collating at accent_stripped tier -- a referent/scene shift inside one continuing divine speech, not an addressee drop; the proposed field repair must be re-cut to name that shift, with the PE mark as corroboration, and the docket must judge whether it qualifies as a ruled scene shift explicit in the bytes. Residual, flagged not ruled: with no addressee change at 41.29|42.1, the tier-1-bounded speech from the summons at oshb:Isa.41.21 to the frame at 42.5 is a byte-grounded rival grouping that the neighbouring row dismisses as texture; that is a local seam question, not a book-level one, and this item carries no span proposal. Not a span item.

The shipped strongest_rejected_alternative declines the 42:1-4 continuation 'since the fresh divine-speech-frame formula at oshb:Isa.42.5 is the book's ordinary marker for a new unit, and a parashah PE mark closes the preceding span immediately before it, at oshb:Isa.42.4' -- two coordinate because-grounds, and no digit anywhere in the row for the typicality clause. Byte re-sweep with the object named (the koh-amar formula, skeleton tier, verse counts): 48 verses book-wide; within chs 41-43 exactly 4 (MT 42:5, 43:1, 43:14, 43:16), 0 in ch 41; all four divine-owned by their own bytes -- כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר הָאֵ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.42.5, tier: byte), כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.43.1, tier: byte), כֹּֽה אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.43.14, tier: byte), כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.43.16, tier: byte) -- so the auditor's digit is exact, and it is the digit the book-order neighbor row already ships for the identical warrant. Mark inventory: MT 42:4 carries PE (type correct; single-witness disclosed in the row), but prophets-parashah is tier-3 weak corroboration and cannot stand as a because-ground. Tested against the row: the onset itself is sound -- the frame re-collates at byte tier in the cited verse and is tier-1 on its own -- so the refusal survives on the frame alone and the defect is confined to the warrant field; not load-bearing, so not high. One nuance the finding does not state: the staged universals checker does not lexicon 'ordinary', so this is a typicality-standard judgment rather than a mechanical gate failure; it still qualifies as a defective warrant because the identical claim carries the mandated sweep in the neighbor row and because the tier-3 mark is presented as a coordinate ground. Medium stands.

items.claim: The row's back-seam warrant names a fear-not formula as the onset signal at web:Isa.44.1, but no fear-not formula stands in that verse's bytes in either witness.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways. MT 44:1 in full is וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier): no fear-not stands in it -- the pair skeleton אל תירא is absent from the verse at skeleton tier and no token carries the verb skeleton תירא (skeleton tier) -- and WEB 44:1 reads “Yet listen now, Jacob my servant, and Israel, whom I have chosen.” (web:Isa.44.1). The formula stands one verse later, אַל תִּירָא֙ (oshb:Isa.44.2, byte tier); a byte-tier sweep of that exact pointed pair returns 4 verses (MT 37:6, 41:10, 43:1, 44:2; count object: pointed two-token form, verse count), so the auditor's 43:1 identity claim holds at byte tier. The named-servant half of the descriptor is byte-true at 44:1: יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier). The book-order neighbour row places the koh-amar frame and the fear-not it governs 'one verse inside the unit rather than at the onset', so the two rows do locate one formula at two verses. The seam survives without the misplaced formula: the adversative-plus-imperative onset וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע (oshb:Isa.44.1, byte tier), whose first token matches MT 43:1's וְעַתָּ֞ה (oshb:Isa.43.1, byte tier) at accent-stripped tier only; the verdict close at web:Isa.43.28; and the setumah after MT 43:28 (tier-3, single-witness, confirmed in the inventory). items.claim: The same byte construction is load-bearing in opposite directions inside this batch without a stated principle: a verse-initial conjunction plus messenger formula is argued here as a reason NOT to cut at web:Isa.56.3 to web:Isa.56.4, while the identical construction is the seam driver at web:Isa.52.3 to web:Isa.52.4 in the rows that ship the preceding spans.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes, both ways. MT 56:4 opens כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier): the conjunction is token 1 and the formula tokens 2-4, so the row's statement that the 56:4 formula is not verse-initial and stands after a subordinating conjunction is byte-true. Sweep of the skeleton כי כה אמר (skeleton tier): 14 verses, 14 tokens, word-bound and substring counts agreeing, so the finding's digit re-derives; but its 'one object book-wide' framing blends the role split the hazard catalog forbids blending: MT 36:16 is one of the 14 and is a royal-messenger site per the koh-amar census (royal sites exactly 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, 37:3), standing mid-verse, while the divine-frame verse-initial object stands in 13 verses (8:11, 18:4, 21:6, 21:16, 30:15, 31:4, 45:18, 49:25, 52:3, 52:4, 56:4, 57:15, 66:12), the three named among them. What is verifiable against the shipped row: no field names a principle that lets a conjunction-prefixed formula reinforce an open frame here while opening one elsewhere, although a byte-visible discriminator sits in the row's own span and goes unstated: the formula's addressee לַסָּֽרִיסִים֙ (oshb:Isa.56.4, byte tier) resumes the party the preceding verse quotes, וְאַל יֹאמַר֙ הַסָּרִ֔יס (oshb:Isa.56.3, byte tier), a lexical tie on the skeleton סריס (oshb:Isa.56.3 and oshb:Isa.56.4, skeleton tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide, 39:7, 56:3, 56:4), and the frame-owner is the same tetragrammaton form at כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.56.1, byte tier) and 56:4, whereas 52:4 shifts to the adonai-YHWH form. Tested against the neighbor evidence readable here, the row's treatment is coherent rather than incoherent: the row shipping MT 57:14-57:21 in this slice's context likewise declines to open at the conjunction-prefixed frame כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר רָ֣ם וְנִשָּׂ֗א (oshb:Isa.57.15, byte tier). The cross-row half of the claim, that the rows shipping MT 52:3-52:4 treat this construction as a fresh onset at 52:3|52:4, cannot be re-derived here: those rows lie outside this slice's context and no exact path to them was supplied, so that assertion stands on the auditor's report alone; the mark inventory keys only a SAMEKH at MT 52:2 (single-witness, tier-3) near that seam and no seg at 52:3 or 52:4. On the evidence in hand the surviving defect is an unstated discriminating principle inside a warrant that is byte-true and not load-bearing, since the hold across 56:3 and 56:4 also rests on the byte-identical refrain pairs the row discloses, שֹׁמֵ֤ר שַׁבָּת֙ מֵֽחַלְּל֔וֹ (oshb:Isa.56.2 and oshb:Isa.56.6, byte tier; 2 verses book-wide) and וּמַחֲזִיקִ֖ים בִּבְרִיתִֽי (oshb:Isa.56.4 and oshb:Isa.56.6, byte tier; 2 verses book-wide). items.claim: The row's span-cohesion warrant — that first-person-plural verb forms continue through web:Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14 — overreaches its own bytes by two verses.

(web:Isa.59.14). items.claim: The row's sole front-seam signal, a first-person resolve onset, does not discriminate the seam and is neither spliced nor disclosed as continuous across it.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): splice לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה and לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) as the named onset, disclose that the first-person-singular voice straddles the front seam from oshb:Isa.61.10, and re-state what actually discriminates the seam (the lamed-purpose Zion/Jerusalem vow) — observed_substrate_signals and confidence are dependent fields of that restatement.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. First-person-singular (1cs) forms run through the verse before the seam: שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), נַפְשִׁי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), בֵּֽאלֹהַ֔י (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), הִלְבִּישַׁ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) and יְעָטָ֑נִי (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) are a 1cs verb and 1cs suffixes; the same utterance continues through the simile כֵּ֣ן אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה יַצְמִ֤יחַ (oshb:Isa.61.11, byte tier), a verse carrying no first-person form at all, and the 1cs voice resumes at the row's own onset in the two lamed-purpose vow clauses לְמַ֤עַן צִיּוֹן֙ לֹ֣א אֶחֱשֶׁ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier) and וּלְמַ֥עַן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לֹ֣א אֶשְׁק֑וֹט (oshb:Isa.62.1, byte tier), both 1cs imperfects. The row discloses first-person continuity across its rear seam (62:5|62:6) but says nothing about the same continuity across its own front seam, while the book-order neighbor row argues this very seam as a rhetorical-mode shift with the person unchanged. Tested the other way, against the finding: the seam itself is sound, since the report-to-vow shift at the lamed-purpose clauses is real in the bytes, and the paragraph-mark inventory (single witness) carries no parashah mark at MT 61:10, 61:11 or 62:1 (MT 61:11 holds a paseq seg, count-layer only), so the row's no-mark statement is accurate and no tier-3 corroboration is misreported in either direction. The defect is therefore a defective front-seam warrant (its only signal is a feature continuous across the seam, and the feature that does discriminate is unevidenced in the row) plus undisclosed cross-seam person continuity, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

Second-person-feminine-singular (2fs) address runs unbroken from צִדְקֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier), כְּבוֹדֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) and לָךְ֙ (oshb:Isa.62.2, byte tier) through וְהָיִ֛יתְ (oshb:Isa.62.3, byte tier) and אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.3, byte tier), בָּ֔ךְ וְאַרְצֵ֖ךְ (oshb:Isa.62.4, byte tier), יִבְעָל֖וּךְ בָּנָ֑יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) and עָלַ֖יִךְ אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.5, byte tier) into the row's own opening token pair עַל חוֹמֹתַ֣יִךְ (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) (2fs suffix), after which the vocative יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) stands as the verse's third token, naming the addressee already under address rather than opening a new one; the first change of addressee inside the row is the second-person-masculine-plural charge אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), which the row does disclose as intra-span alternation. Tested the other way, against the finding: the vocative is explicit in the bytes (a tier-1 class where explicit), and the seam survives on the new completed first-person act with a new participant group, הִפְקַ֨דְתִּי֙ שֹֽׁמְרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier), so the placement stands; the defect is undisclosed cross-seam address continuity together with an addressee-shift framing the bytes do not support, a defective warrant that is not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): re-argue the rear seam on the verse-initial doubled imperative and the content turn to highway preparation, dropping the 'unnamed group' ground so the seam is argued compatibly from both sides.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. Plural address is already live before the seam: הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) identifies the addressees by a participle, and אַל דֳּמִ֖י לָכֶֽם (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) plus וְאַֽל תִּתְּנ֥וּ (oshb:Isa.62.7, byte tier) are second-person-masculine-plural (2mp) forms. MT 62:10 then carries six 2mp imperatives with no addressee named anywhere in the verse: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), פַּנּ֖וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סֹ֣לּוּ סֹ֤לּוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier), סַקְּל֣וּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) and הָרִ֥ימוּ (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier). The bytes thus establish a content turn (from the charge to give Yahweh no rest to gate, highway and banner commands) under an unbroken 2mp address; they cannot establish that the 62:10 group differs from the 62:6-7 group, which is what the row's ground 'addressed to an unnamed group rather than continuing the charge just laid on the watchmen' asserts. The book-order neighbor row argues the identical seam as 'not a shift to an unnamed addressee but a shift in content' and repeats the rejection in its rejected alternative, so the two rows carry incompatible warrants for one seam, and the neighbor's framing is the one the bytes support. One overstatement in the finding is noted without effect on the verdict: at 62:6 the plural addressees are identified by הַמַּזְכִּרִים֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.62.6, byte tier) whereas at 62:10 they are not, so the group is in fact more unnamed at 62:10; that is a naming fact, not an addressee change, and the row's warrant still asserts a discontinuity the bytes cannot carry. The seam survives on the doubled verse-initial imperative and the content turn, with a SAMEKH at MT 62:9 in the paragraph-mark inventory (single witness, tier 3), so this is a defective warrant, not a boundary defect: medium as filed.

items.claim: The rear-seam driver — a Hebrew form-class claim about MT 62:10 — is carried on the English witness alone.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair: splice עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) beside the WEB citation and add oshb:Isa.62.10 to boundary_evidence_refs.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from the shipped row and the bytes. The row's rear-seam sentence carries the Hebrew form-class claim 'a fresh plural-imperative summons' with only the English witness “Go through, go through the gates!” (web:Isa.62.10), which does not mark number; its boundary_evidence_refs pair an oshb entry with every other web verse they cite (62:6, 62:7, 62:8, 62:9 as a setumah entry) but carry no oshb:Isa.62.10, and no Hebrew from that verse appears in any field of the row. The claim itself is byte-true: עִבְר֤וּ עִבְרוּ֙ בַּשְּׁעָרִ֔ים (oshb:Isa.62.10, byte tier) opens the verse with a doubled 2mp imperative, and the book-order neighbor row splices exactly this run at byte tier for the same seam. Under the engagement-class rule a form-class label on a seam driver is a byte-checkable claim carrying the same discipline as a digit and requiring a pointed splice with its tier named, so a rear-seam driver carried on the English witness alone is an unsupported warrant as shipped rather than a mechanical omission; it is not load-bearing beyond repair because the claim re-derives true and the seam is independently secured by the neighbor row's splice and the SAMEKH at MT 62:9 (single witness, tier 3): medium as filed.

items.claim: The rear-seam warrant is byte-false: MT 63:7 does not open a first-person-plural recital, and no change of grammatical person occurs across the seam.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH already disclosed at MT 63:6): delete the 'first-person-plural recital' ground, re-argue the seam as a change of speech-act at unchanged grammatical person, splice חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), add oshb:Isa.63.7 to boundary_evidence_refs, and re-test confidence and frontier_flag now that the person-shift ground is withdrawn.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 63:6 closes in the first-person singular (1cs): וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) and וְאוֹרִ֥יד (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) are 1cs verbs with a 1cs suffix. MT 63:7 opens חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) with a first-person SINGULAR hiphil imperfect, rendered “I will tell of the loving kindnesses of Yahweh” (web:Isa.63.7); the verse's only first-person-plural element is the object suffix in גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), and it contains no first-person-plural verb, so the row's 'a first-person-plural recital of Yahweh's mercies replaces the divine warrior's own first-person report' is byte-false as a person contrast: grammatical person is unchanged across the seam, exactly as the book-order neighbor row states. The row also cites web:Isa.63.7 with no oshb:Isa.63.7 entry and no splice from the verse its rear seam turns on, and ships at confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false. The finding is confirmed as to fact; the filed severity is not. Tested the other way, against the row's own seam: the divine name stands in the third person three times under that 1cs verb, in חַֽסְדֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אַזְכִּיר֙ (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), תְּהִלֹּ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier) and גְּמָלָ֖נוּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.63.7, byte tier), which by itself separates the 63:7 speaker from the warrior who at וְאָב֤וּס עַמִּים֙ בְּאַפִּ֔י (oshb:Isa.63.6, byte tier) reports his own deeds; the speech-act change (recital versus action report) is byte-grounded at the same verb; MT 63:7 carries no interrogative, so the row's 'no further interrogative sustaining the dialogue frame' is byte-true; and the paragraph-mark inventory records a SAMEKH at MT 63:6 (single witness, tier 3; MT 63:7 holds only a count-layer paseq seg). The seam therefore survives with the person-shift descriptor deleted, which the finding's own proposed change concedes ('the seam itself survives on the speech-act change and the tier-3 SAMEKH'). Under the severity law a byte-false claim is high only where it is load-bearing; this descriptor is one of four grounds in the rear-seam sentence and the boundary at 63:6|63:7 does not depend on it, so it is a defective warrant claim not alone load-bearing: downgraded to medium, with the missing oshb:Isa.63.7 engagement and the unrevisited high confidence noted as aggravating but not boundary-affecting.

items.claim: The row's prose carries two bare, witness-unqualified chapter-and-verse coordinates inside offset zone B, where the same numerals denote different verses in the two witnesses.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair: qualify both prose coordinates (web:Isa.64.2-Isa.64.3 (MT 64:1-64:2) and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4)) to match the disclosure already used elsewhere in the row.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes and the staged crosswalk; every run below collates at byte tier. The row's boundary_rationale writes 'mountains quaking again at 64:2-3' and its strongest_rejected_alternative 'the confessional turn at 64:5' with no witness prefix and no numeric qualifier, inside zone B where the crosswalk maps WEB 64:2, 64:3 and 64:5 to MT 64:1, 64:2 and 64:4. Under the book-wide convention that bare coordinates are WEB, both are content-correct: web:Isa.64.2 (MT 64:1) carries the kindling fire and the trembling nations, כִּקְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier) and מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier); web:Isa.64.3 (MT 64:2) carries the second mountain-quaking report יָרַ֕דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier); and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4) carries the confession הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). Read as MT numbers they fail: oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4 opens וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier) and runs to the incomparability affirmation עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), not a quaking report, and MT 64:5 = web:Isa.64.6 is a different confession verse. So the defect is real: two zone-B coordinates in prose do not name their numbering space, against the rule that any digit touching chs 63-64 names it, in the row that carries the split verse and that otherwise dual-qualifies every structured ref. Tested the other way, against the finding: nothing in the row is byte-false, both coordinates resolve correctly under the governing convention, the row's boundary_evidence_refs and device_notes carry arithmetically correct duals, and no seam depends on either coordinate; the ambiguity is one of labeling, which the severity law places at low (disclosure shortfall), not a defective digit claim. Noted without effect on the verdict: the finding's own Hebrew citations are unfilled percent-s placeholders, so its byte grounds were re-derived here rather than trusted. Downgraded to low.

items.claim: The rear-seam warrant presents the confessional turn as opening web:Isa.64.5, but that verse opens on continuing second-person praise; the confession begins only after the verse's own caesura.
items.auditor_proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement; web:Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3 remains the last verse boundary available before the turn): disclose that the confessional turn stands mid-verse in oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, after that verse's own caesura, and state the seam as the nearest verse boundary before it.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 64:4 (= web:Isa.64.5 by the crosswalk) carries its athnach (U+0591) on its seventh token יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier); the half before it, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), is a 2ms verb with 2ms suffixes continuing the address to Yahweh from עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), rendered “You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember you in your ways.” (web:Isa.64.5); the self-accusation הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), whose וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier) is the verse's first first-person-plural form, stands only after that caesura, rendered “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5). The row closes 'immediately before the confessional turn ... (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act' and its rejected alternative treats 'the confessional turn at 64:5' as the whole verse's mode, so the rear-seam driver is presented as verse-initial when half a verse of the row's own second-person petition mode intervenes between the row's close and the turn; the book-order neighbor row discloses the mid-verse onset explicitly and this row does not. Tested the other way, against the finding: rows are verse-granular, web:Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3 is the nearest verse boundary before the turn, and the paragraph-mark inventory carries no mark at MT 64:3 or 64:4, so the placement stands and no respan is implied; the defect is a mis-presented driver position in a medium_low, frontier-flagged row whose seam is argued from exactly that rhetorical-mode shift, a defective warrant not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

items.claim: The front-seam warrant's own contrast is not byte-supported: the 'second-person address' versus 'first-person-plural admission' opposition fails because the second half of the same verse opens on second-person address too, and first-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived at byte tier from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 (14 tokens; atnach on token 7, יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ): the second half opens on הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ (tokens 8-10), second-person address in the same person as the first half's opening verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (token 1), so the person of address does not change across the caesura; the only new element is the first-person-plural confession verb וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (token 11), WEB “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4). First-person-plural verbs already stand inside the preceding row's span: הָיִ֗ינוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, token 1; WEB “We have become”) and נְקַוֶּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, token 4; WEB “we didn’t look for”) -- no morphology layer is staged, so the form class rests on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. Tested the other way, the row's underlying seam fact holds: skeleton-tier sweeps of the sin, iniquity and transgression roots spliced from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, oshb:Isa.64.5 = web:Isa.64.6 and oshb:Isa.59.20 return 23, 16 and 18 verses book-wide with none inside oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.3 (= web:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.4), so the confession onset at oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 survives and the finding is right to leave the span alone. The warrant's stated contrast (second-person address versus first-person-plural admission) is byte-defective as a distinguishing ground, while the seam does not rest on that contrast alone: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (rest the contrast on the confession verb alone and drop the person-shift framing) is consistent with the bytes.

items.claim: The rear-seam hinge device -- 'a final unanswered double question', carried into observed_substrate_signals as speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question -- is established only from the WEB rendering's two question marks; the row carries no Hebrew splice or accent citation at its own closing verse, where a single interrogative particle governs both clauses across the caesura.

Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12 = oshb:Isa.64.11) with two question marks, and that WEB run is the row's only citation for its 'final unanswered double question' and for the observed_substrate_signals entry speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question: the row splices no Hebrew at its own closing verse and none at oshb:Isa.65.1, whose verse-initial first-person form נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙ (byte tier) is the actual tier-1 speaker change it invokes. Tested the other way, the closure survives on the bytes (the interrogative particle, the first-person reply at oshb:Isa.65.1, and the SAMEKH the inventory records at MT 64:11 -- single-witness, tier-3), so the seam is not load-bearing on the punctuation; but a seam-relevant device whose 'double' count is a translation-punctuation fact and whose closing verse carries no pointed splice is a defective warrant under the tier-4 law: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (splice the particle and atnach position, or re-label the signal key) is consistent with the bytes.
